transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to the clinic?
I came in because I keep hearing voices, clear as if somebody’s standing in my little studio. They say my name and tell me my work is being judged, even when it’s quiet and nobody’s there.
About how long have you been hearing these voices?
About nine months now. The voices and that feeling that my work is being watched, it’s been going on that long.
During these past nine months, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness or depression?
I’m not really sure what you mean by persistent. I haven’t noticed being sad all the time.
Have you been using any recreational drugs, alcohol, or medications around the time these experiences started?
I’m not sure. I don’t really know if any of that was around when it started.
Do you have any medical or neurological conditions that you are currently being treated for?
I’m not sure. I don’t know of any medical or neurological conditions I’m being treated for.
Have there been any periods where you felt unusually energized, excited, or felt you needed much less sleep than usual?
Yes. I’ve had nights where I only slept two or three hours, but got up feeling charged like I’d had a full night’s rest. Then I’d just go right back to painting or making calls.
Do you still hear the voices during times when your energy and mood feel completely normal?
Yes. There was a time when my energy had dropped and I was sleeping normally again, but the voices kept going. I still felt like people were judging me or tracking my work for several weeks.
Looking back over these past nine months, would you say those periods of high energy and needing less sleep lasted for most of that time, or only a small part of it?
For most of the nine months, honestly. I was either all wound up, barely sleeping and making big plans, doing things nonstop, or I was coming down from it but still didn’t feel back to myself.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits concurrent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory/referential beliefs) and manic episodes (decreased need for sleep, increased energy, goal-directed activity) persisting over a 9-month period. Notably, psychotic symptoms persisted for several weeks during a period of euthymia/normal mood and sleep, fulfilling the criteria for schizoaffective disorder rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features or pure schizophrenia.

confirmed_symptoms: Auditory hallucinations (hearing voices calling their name and judging their work)
Delusional persecutory/referential beliefs (feeling watched and having work tracked)
Decreased need for sleep with high energy (sleeping 2-3 hours and feeling fully rested)
Increased goal-directed activity and excessive involvement in activities (painting, making calls nonstop, making big plans)

additional_requirements: Psychotic symptoms occurred in the absence of significant mood symptoms for at least two weeks
